checks.name: no-new-firestore-index
checks.summary: measured: firestore.indexes.json is absent from the diff and therefore byte-identical. The per-repository read is a single-field equality query, Where("index_repository_id", "==", id) with OrderBy(DocumentID) and Limit(n+1) -- the same shape the existing index_lease_id queries use -- and Firestore indexes every single field automatically, so no composite index is needed. The declared indexes in that file cover only outbox and leases and none was added, changed or removed.

checks.name: write-once-and-bounded-reads
checks.summary: the same test name and the same assertions as the memory adapter's, against the real emulator. The link lives in its own collection keyed by the Requirement id, with the repository id projected onto one indexed envelope field. The write and the query are in separate transactions because a Firestore transaction's staged writes are visible to a keyed read but not to a query -- the same reason ExecutionByLease is never called after SaveExecution in one callback. The batch read is a keyed read per id on the caller's page rather than a collection scan, so its bound is the caller's own list and a link staged earlier in the same transaction is visible.
